subject: BlueFjord renewal: price-hold vs incremental commit options
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily@bluefjord.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@bluefjord.io>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion: keeping rate stable or move to commit?

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the Q1 usage export — attached for reference (we pulled it from our side as well). BlueFjord's board is asking for clarity on renewal economics. We're looking at a 12-month renewal that also expands capacity for a new feature team (roughly +30% token volume). Two things they're debating:

- A one-year price-hold (keep current token rates) with a modest uplift in committed volume, or
- A more aggressive committed-usage contract (18-month term) with a deeper discount and a small upfront credit.

Can you outline pros/cons from Redwood's side (latency/availability guarantees, burst allowances, and any credit mechanics)? If you can send a sample term-sheet showing both options, that would help the procurement team.

Also, can you confirm whether we could keep burst capacity for seasonal traffic without triggering overage immediately?

Thanks — Emily
Emily Chen
Head of Platform, BlueFjord Labs
attachments: BlueFjord_USAGE_Q1_2027.csv

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@bluefjord.io>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@bluefjord.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: keeping rate stable or move to commit?

Hi Emily / Tom — thanks for the clear framing and the usage file. Looping Ben and Laura for commercial + legal visibility.

High level: both approaches are workable. Practical trade-offs are below — I'll attach a draft term sheet (term_sheet_BF_v3.pdf) and a one-page SOW for the capacity uplift.

Option A: 12-month price-hold + modest commit
- Keep current per-token price for 12 months.
- Customer ups the committed baseline by ~30% to cover new team.
- Redwood provides a burst buffer (20% above committed baseline) with graduated overage pricing for sustained overage beyond a defined monthly threshold.
- Minimal upfront credit.
- Pros for BlueFjord: immediate predictability on unit price, simpler procurement.
- Cons for BlueFjord: smaller discount compared to longer commit; limited protection if usage grows >40%.

Option B: 18-month heavier commit + upfront credit
- 10–15% effective discount on per-token rate if the customer commits to the higher baseline for 18 months.
- Redwood issues a one-time credit (applied to first invoice) to offset migration/onboarding work.
- Burst policy remains; longer term allows Redwood to reserve capacity more efficiently (better SLOs during peak).
- Pros for BlueFjord: deeper unit economics and predictable capacity; cons: longer term commitment, larger true-up complexity if they miss commit.

Technical / ops notes:
- Burst handling: we can keep burst active. Short spikes (minutes-hours) are absorbed by the burst buffer and billed at an overage rate only if sustained beyond the monthly threshold.
- SLA: for dedicated capacity options we can add a 99.9% availability target (can be incorporated as an addendum).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Ben/Laura and I finalize numbers in the attached term sheet (two scenarios spelled out).
2) BlueFjord picks preferred option and we lock in a mutual action plan (milestones, migration window, SOW sign-off).
3) Procurement loop to review contract language and any SOC-2 evidence asks.

I've attached: term_sheet_BF_v3.pdf and SOW_bluefjord_upgrade_draft.docx.

Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the trade-offs if useful.

Best,
Priyom
Director, Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
attachments: term_sheet_BF_v3.pdf, SOW_bluefjord_upgrade_draft.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Apr 2027 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: BlueFjord margin math and recommended concessions (do not externalize yet)

Team — quick internal note on the two options Priyom outlined. Numbers above assume current blended token economics; I ran the sensitivity on a few scenarios (see attached internal calc).

Key points:
- Option A (12m price-hold + +30% commit): minimal downside to Redwood if BlueFjord stays within +30–40% year-over-year growth. Margins compress ~4–6% vs baseline.
- Option B (18m commit, deeper discount + upfront credit): gives a 10–12% uplift in committed revenue stability; margin hit on year-1 ~7–9% but we capture renewal optionality and reduce churn risk.

Recommendation: offer Option B but with a capped credit (one-time equal to ~1 month of current MSU) and an operational guardrail: include a staged true-up (quarterly) with a 60-day remediation window before penalties. Also require BlueFjord to commit to a minimum monthly baseline for months 1–6.

If we externalize this, push the credit as onboarding support (engineering uplift + data migration) rather than a price concession. Laura — can legal draft the clause for staged true-up and remediation?

-Ben

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@bluefjord.io>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@bluefjord.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Apr 2027 11:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: keeping rate stable or move to commit?

Hi Emily / Tom — following up with the updated term sheet reflecting the recommended commercial guardrails. Highlights:

- Option 1 (12m price-hold + +30% commit): identical to prior note.
- Option 2 (preferred): 18m commit with a 12% unit discount and a one-time onboarding credit equal to ~1 month of current spend (applied to invoice 1). Staged true-up: quarterly measurements with a 60-day remediation window before any surcharge.

Operationally we'll:
- Keep a 20% burst buffer for short spikes.
- Provide a Playbook for spike detection and auto-burst handling (ops team will share runbooks).
- Include a short technical migration checklist in the SOW.

Can you confirm which option BlueFjord prefers and whether procurement needs any changes to the phrasing around the credit (we can present it as an onboarding support credit to make approval easier). If you'd like, let's schedule procurement + legal call next week.

Thanks,
Priyom

Tom
